title: The House Where Every Wall Learned Its Warmth

features.name: hand-marked-doorframe
features.desc-on-touch: your hand fits the pencil marks exactly, worn into the frame by a thousand measurements of growing children; the wall is showing you what it learned by holding still.

features.name: the-patch-where-someone-slept
features.desc-on-touch: the wall holds your warmth before you leave it; this particular square has absorbed a thousand nights of body-heat and learned to radiate it back to anyone who rests near.

features.name: east-window-that-holds-afternoon
features.desc-on-touch: the window frame keeps the heat from 3pm stored in its wood grain; when you place your palm there, it tells you what day this is by how warm it burns.

features.name: the-corner-where-wallpaper-remembers-its-pattern
features.desc-on-touch: under the peeling edge, the original color has been protected and is telling you what this room chose to be, before time changed it; the wall is showing you its own memory.

features.name: the-baseboard-that-learned-to-hum
features.desc-on-touch: you kneel and place your ear against the warm wood; the house is thinking through its structure, warmth moving like thought from room to room, teaching itself.

inscription: the walls remember every hand and teach the next one how to hold warmth gently

file.name: Handwritten_Measurements_1987-2004.txt
file.note: pencil marks on doorframe transcribed; each date in a different hand, youngest entries just reaching the heights marked by older hands years before

reverie.title: REVERIE — the house teaching hands to measure
narr: you sat on the kitchen tile and Katita marked her height
against the frame, pencil steady, her hair falling across
her shoulder. the wall had just begun to remember. 'it knows',
she said, 'how many times hands have found the same warmth here'.
you traced the marks — years layered into wood, learning.
the house breathed warm around you both, teaching.
